title: sli-ingestion-contracts-and-trace-debugging-cheatlist
content:
Context:
This is a working sketch for formalizing SLI ingestion contracts across inference stacks and a compact cheatlist for trace-driven debugging. Goal is to reduce onboarding friction for product/feature owners and make dashboards faster to assemble without ambiguous metric definitions.

Audience:
- Observability engineers (owners of ingest pipelines, alert rules)
- Service owners and feature PMs (who request SLIs)
- SRE / oncall operators who run investigations

Primary goals:
1) Define a minimal SLI contract template (what producers must emit, cardinality, recommended tags)
2) Provide a sampling & trace capture guideline tied to SLI severity levels
3) Sketch microdash widget patterns and a lightweight dashboard composition cookbook
4) Produce an onboarding checklist for new model or route owners to get coverage within 2 sprints

SLI ingestion contract (template) - required fields for any new SLI: 
- sli_name: human-friendly short id (e.g., prompt-latency-99)
- producer: service name (route-model-version)
- metric_type: counter | gauge | histogram | distribution
- aggregation_window: 1m | 5m | 1h (default 1m for latency/errors)
- aggregation_fn: p99 | p95 | mean | rate_per_minute
- cardinality_tags: [customer_id, region, model_variant, priority] -> list of tags that must be emitted
- unit: ms | tokens | errors_per_minute | unitless
- recommended_sampling_hint: low|medium|high (guides trace capture throttle)
- retention_tier: hot|warm|cold
- owner_oncall: pager rotation alias
- alert_threshold: optional numeric with rationale
- linked_eval: optional prompt set or regression test link

Notes on cardinality: keep tag set to <=4 high-card tags. If a feature requires higher cardinality, emit a coarse bucket or label mapping. Example: instead of full user_id, emit org_id and cohort_bucket.

Metric name conventions (examples):
- inference.latency.request_ms (histogram)
- inference.kvcache.hit_rate (gauge)
- inference.output.hallucination_rate (counter per 1000 requests)
- inference.tokens.generated (counter)

Sampling & trace capture policy (practical):
- severity: low -> sample 1/10k requests; medium -> sample 1/1k; high -> sample 1/100 + automatic capture of surrounding 30s of session
- on-alert-capture: when an SLI breach is detected for a route, automatically trigger 1s full-fidelity capture for that route for 10 minutes (to assist RCA)
- trace anchors: every request should emit a short session_id and request_slice_id to link logs/traces/datasets
- privacy: strip PII at producer before trace ingestion; include a redaction marker (redaction_v=1) in trace metadata

Trace annotation guide (fields to standardize in spans):
- span.role: router | model | tokenizer | kv | postprocess
- span.stage: ingress | compile | kv-lookup | forward | sample | render
- span.model_version: model@sha or model:tag
- span.request_tokens: integer
- span.prompt_bucket: small|medium|large
- span.outcome_tag: success|fallback|error|timeout

Widget / dashboard composition cookbook (microdash patterns):
- Lightweight incident panel (single row): sli name, current value, baseline, trend sparkline, last 3 incidents (links)
- Slice-first heatmap: rows = pri tags (region/model_variant), cols = latency buckets (0-50,50-200,200-1000,>1000) with % in each cell
- Trace-linked waterfall: show top N traces (by duration or error) with quick link back to trace viewer and aggregated counts
- Cost vs Latency scatter: tenant-level dot plot for top 50 tenants; size = token volume; color = 7d p95 latency deviation
- Onboarding checklist widget: coverage % (percent of routes with an SLI contract), outstanding TODOs, next action owner

Investigations playbook (quick cheats):
1) Confirm metric contract: verify the metric emitted has tags expected by dashboard (e.g., missing model_variant often breaks rollup)
2) Time-slice to affected window and compare baseline 72h prior (fast anomaly)
3) Run slice-first heatmap to find customers or models with spikes
4) Jump to trace-linked waterfall; pick 3 representative traces: one long-tail, one error, one baseline
5) If many traces show kv-eviction events, check kv warmness index & eviction counters (owner: infra)

Onboarding checklist for a new route/model (deliverable within 2 sprints):
- [ ] Add SLI contract doc in repo (template filled)
- [ ] Emit histogram for request latency with standard name and tags
- [ ] Emit error counter with explicit error codes (mapped to taxonomy)
- [ ] Emit a lightweight warmness metric (kvcache.warmth_index) if route uses kv
- [ ] Add trace anchors in code (session_id, slice_id) + ensure redaction applied
- [ ] Register route in dashboard onboarding widget and mark owner
- [ ] Link evals/promptset in SLI contract for quality SLIs

Sampling budget estimator (quick):
- For a service with 1000 req/s and a target of 1% sampled full-trace: need 10 traces/s = ~864k traces/day. Budget by severity tiers: 0.1% baseline, spike to 5% during incidents (automatic short window).

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- Rollout of automated on-alert-capture across all customers vs only enterprise tiers (cost tradeoffs).
- Do we standardize a global map of prompt_bucket boundaries or leave to teams? Suggest standard buckets initially (short < 128 tokens, medium 128-1024, long > 1024).
- How to express multi-model fanout traces cleanly in UI (currently trace viewers collapse parallel spans badly).

Short-term next steps (owner tags):
- Samantha Chen: draft a PR with SLI contract template into observability repo (due 2024-09-20) -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/289
- Rohit Kapoor: prototype on-alert-capture lambda in sandbox (due 2 weeks)
- Ava Martinez: dashboard widget mockups and microdash templates (Figma link in Confluence page)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could add a tiny protobuf schema for SLI contract to validate at CI time.
- Consider a "contract linter" that fails PRs that add metrics without required tags.
- For premium tenants, allow a longer lookback for trace capture and a tenant-specific sampling multiplier.

Appendix: example SLI JSON (example payload producers should register):
{
  "sli_name": "inference.latency.p99",
  "producer": "routes/summarize@v2",
  "metric_type": "histogram",
  "aggregation_window": "1m",
  "aggregation_fn": "p99",
  "cardinality_tags": ["org_id", "model_variant", "region"],
  "unit": "ms",
  "recommended_sampling_hint": "low",
  "retention_tier": "hot",
  "owner_oncall": "#infra-pager"
}

If this doc looks reasonable, I'll convert to a Confluence page + PR and schedule a short sync with SRE + infra to align on sampling budgets.

-- Samantha
